anglo-american-axis.New York hub: Home of the New York Fed and of the banks that hold most of its stock.
anglo-american-axis.London partner: The Bank of England and the London banks tied to the New York houses.
anglo-american-axis.foreign parent of a holder: A foreign company whose US bank holds New York Fed stock.

central-bankers-clubs.host: Hosts the offices or meetings of these clubs.
central-bankers-clubs.BIS founding shareholder: Its central bank took founding shares in the Bank for International Settlements.
central-bankers-clubs.forum conflict finding: An official watchdog found a problem with a central banker's membership of a private forum.

cfa-franc-zone.guarantor: Its treasury holds the deposit accounts and guarantees that the franc converts into euros.
cfa-franc-zone.West African union (reformed 2019-20): Uses the West African franc issued by the BCEAO. Since January 2020 the bank no longer has to deposit reserves at the French Treasury.
cfa-franc-zone.Central African union (50% deposit): Uses the Central African franc issued by the BEAC, which must deposit at least 50% of its reserves at the French Treasury.
cfa-franc-zone.Comoros (65% deposit): Has its own agreement with France, with a 65% deposit requirement.

banknote-printer-bribery.central bank owned the printer: Its central bank owned a printing firm involved in bribery abroad.
banknote-printer-bribery.private printer's home: Home country of a private printing firm named in these cases.
banknote-printer-bribery.client central bank: A central bank that bought banknotes from a printer in a documented bribery case.

finance-revolving-door.both directions: Documented officials both came to the bank from private finance and left it for private finance.
finance-revolving-door.inflow from finance: Documented officials came to the bank from private finance.
finance-revolving-door.outflow to finance: Documented officials left the bank for private finance.

weaponized-reserves.freezing jurisdiction: A government that froze or seized central bank reserves held within its reach.
weaponized-reserves.reserves frozen: A country whose central bank reserves were frozen or seized abroad.
weaponized-reserves.intended recipient: A country meant to receive money from another country's frozen reserves.

swap-line-blocs.hub: The center of a network: the Federal Reserve or the People's Bank of China, lending its own currency to partners.
swap-line-blocs.Fed standing line: Has a permanent line to borrow dollars from the Fed, with no end date.
swap-line-blocs.Fed temporary line only: Had a line from the Fed in a crisis (2008-2010 or 2020-2021). It has expired.
swap-line-blocs.PBoC swap partner: Can borrow renminbi from the People's Bank of China under a swap agreement, and has no Fed line in the groups above.

gulf-dollar-pegs.anchor: The country whose currency and Treasury bonds the Gulf pegs lean on.
gulf-dollar-pegs.dollar peg: Holds its currency at a fixed rate to the US dollar.
gulf-dollar-pegs.basket: Holds its currency against a mix of currencies, not the dollar alone.

independence-law-wave.1989 first mover: Among the first to pass a law making the central bank more independent, around 1989.
independence-law-wave.post-socialist new law: A former socialist country that wrote a new central bank law after 1989.
independence-law-wave.euro entry (1998): Reform dated 1998, the year the European Central Bank took over monetary policy.
independence-law-wave.West African union 2010 statute: Covered by the BCEAO's 2010 statute, which applies to all its members.

banking-crisis-waves.1980-83 wave: Had a systemic banking crisis starting in 1980-83.
banking-crisis-waves.1994-95 wave: Had a systemic banking crisis starting in 1994-95.
banking-crisis-waves.1997-98 wave: Had a systemic banking crisis starting in 1997-98.
banking-crisis-waves.2007-08 wave: Had a systemic banking crisis starting in 2007-08.

governor-removal-wave.governor removed by decree: The president or government removed the governor outright.
governor-removal-wave.removal attempted or prosecuted: The government tried to remove a governor or brought a legal case, and the person stayed or the matter is open.
governor-removal-wave.forced resignation: A governor resigned, with a documented claim of pressure.
governor-removal-wave.public pressure: A head of government publicly attacked the bank or its governor, with no removal.

lebanon-financial-engineering.scheme centre: Where the scheme ran: Banque du Liban in Beirut.
lebanon-financial-engineering.offshore vehicle: Where the shell company used to take commissions was registered.
lebanon-financial-engineering.property and prosecutions: Money from the scheme went here, or its prosecutors opened a case.
lebanon-financial-engineering.sanctioning state: A government that placed sanctions on the former governor and his associates.

city-of-london-offshore.hub: The United Kingdom, whose financial center connects to these islands.
city-of-london-offshore.overseas territory: A British territory abroad, with its own financial secrecy score.
city-of-london-offshore.Crown dependency: An island under the British Crown but outside the UK, with its own financial secrecy score.

big-four-auditors.Big Four auditor: Audited by Deloitte, EY, KPMG or PwC.
big-four-auditors.state audit office: Audited by a public audit body, not a private firm.
big-four-auditors.Big Four sign-off in a scandal: A Big Four firm signed accounts later at the center of a scandal.
